newsitem.title: ISRAEL: U.S. market influences quarter of Israeli bourse.
newsitem.headline: U.S. market influences quarter of Israeli bourse.

text.p: A quarter of the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange (TASE), as measured by market capitalisation, is influenced directly or indirectly by the U.S. stock market, a study by the TASE released on Wednesday said.
The authors said the 14 arbitrage stocks, including heavyweights like Teva Pharmaceutical Industries and Koor Industries, alone accounted for 17.5 percent of the TASE's market capitalisation.

Of the 14 arbitrage shares, the TASE report found that Teva, Nice Systems and Matav Cable Systems were principally traded in the U.S. Because of that, the U.S. markets led their price movements, the report concluded.
It said Koor, Tadiran Ltd and Elron Electronics Industries were traded equally in both markets and the rest principally in Tel Aviv.
Another 7.5 percent comprised 24 companies with either a subsidiary traded on Wall Street or significant holdings in companies there.

It said among these companies, nine had market valuations considerably under the value of their U.S. trade assets. The biggest was Clal Electronic Industries, which had a market valuation of 1.1 billion shekels, while the market valuations of its holdings in Scitex Corp and ECI Telecom was 1.6 billion shekels.
